questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The mediastinum is divided into superior and inferior by a line joining sternal angle to the ________
questions.explanation: The mediastinum is divided into superior and inferior parts by a transverse plane extending from the sternal angle to the T4-T5 intervertebral disc. The sternal angle lies opposite the T4 vertebra and upper half of T5 in most adults. This plane separates superior from inferior mediastinum and is also a landmark for the superior limit of the pericardium, bifurcation of the pulmonary trunk, origin of the arch of the aorta, and the site where the superior vena cava pierces the pericardium to enter the right atrium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following regions does the trachea lie in?
questions.explanation: The trachea lies in the superior mediastinum.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The trachea lies in the superior mediastinum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with myasthenia gravis was suspected to have a thymoma and a lateral chest X-ray was ordered to confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following regions will you expect to find a mass in?
questions.explanation: Thymomas are tumors of the thymus and are associated with myasthenia gravis. The thymus occupies the superior and anterior mediastinum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures is present in the posterior mediastinum?
questions.explanation: The esophagus is present in the posterior mediastinum. It enters the superior mediastinum between the trachea anteriorly and vertebral column posteriorly, then continues inferiorly into the posterior mediastinum, passes through the diaphragm and opens into the stomach. The thymus is in the superior/anterior mediastinum, the ascending aorta is in the middle mediastinum, and the tracheal bifurcation is in the middle mediastinum.

questions.question: Match the following structures and their locations.
questions.explanation: The source explanation gives the correct matching as A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1: left subclavian artery - superior mediastinum; hemiazygos vein - posterior mediastinum; phrenic nerve - middle mediastinum; sternopericardial ligaments - anterior mediastinum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the mediastinum?

options.text: Heart enclosed in the pericardium occupies the middle mediastinum
Thymus remnants may be present in the middle mediastinum
Posterior boundary of posterior mediastinum corresponds to T1-T4 vertebrae
Lower border of anterior mediastinum extends more inferiorly than posterior mediastinum

questions.correctAnswerText: Heart enclosed in the pericardium occupies the middle mediastinum
questions.explanation: The heart enclosed in the pericardium occupies the middle mediastinum. The middle mediastinum is the broadest part of the inferior mediastinum and contains the pericardium, heart, tracheal bifurcation and corresponding vessels and nerves. Thymus/remnants are in the superior and anterior mediastinum. The posterior mediastinum is bounded posteriorly by the bodies of T5-T12 vertebrae, and its lower border extends more inferiorly than that of the anterior mediastinum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 60-year-old woman was diagnosed with papillary carcinoma thyroid. CT cuts from the middle mediastinum showed metastatic deposits. In this section, which of the following structures will not be visualized?
questions.explanation: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve is not visualized in the middle mediastinum; it lies in the superior mediastinum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures do not pass through the superior thoracic aperture?
questions.explanation: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve does not pass through the superior thoracic aperture. It hooks around the right subclavian artery in the neck and ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove. The source lists structures traversing the thoracic inlet including esophagus, trachea, lung apices with pleura, thymic remnants, brachiocephalic artery, brachiocephalic veins, left common carotid artery, internal thoracic and superior intercostal arteries, first intercostal veins, inferior thyroid veins, left recurrent laryngeal nerve, bilateral phrenic and vagus nerves, sympathetic trunks, first thoracic nerves, sternohyoid, sternothyroid, longus colli and thoracic duct.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with lung cancer was found to have the following finding on his anterior abdominal wall. On examination, you observe that the blood flow in these blood vessels is completely downwards. CT chest showed obstruction of a thoracic vessel. Which of the following is false about the same?

options.text: Pierces the pericardium at 3rd costal cartilage
Enters the heart at the level of 4th intercostal space
Receives azygous vein below sternal angle

questions.correctAnswerText: Pierces the pericardium at 3rd costal cartilage
questions.explanation: The clinical finding is superior vena cava obstruction. The false statement is that the superior vena cava pierces the pericardium at the third costal cartilage. The source places pericardial penetration opposite the second costal cartilage/angle of Louis at the T4-T5 plane. The azygos vein joins about 2 cm below the sternal plane at T5, and the superior vena cava enters the right atrium at the level of the fourth intercostal space. SVC obstruction can cause swelling of the face/neck, dyspnea, headache, dizziness, hemoptysis, dilated neck veins, proptosis, papilledema and prominent anterior chest-wall collateral veins with downward flow.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The thoracic duct usually originates at the level of:
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct usually originates at the L1 level, anterior to L1/L2. The intestinal trunk and two lumbar lymph trunks join to form the cisterna chyli, which continues as the thoracic duct. The duct enters the posterior mediastinum through the aortic hiatus, lies on the right between the aorta and azygos vein until T4-T5, crosses to the left posterior to the esophagus, ascends and arches over the subclavian artery, and drains into the junction of the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins. It drains both halves of the body below the diaphragm and the left half of the head/neck, left upper limb and left thorax above the diaphragm.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The thoracic duct receives tributaries from all of the following except:
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct does not receive the right bronchomediastinal lymphatic trunk; that trunk contributes to the right lymphatic drainage. The source describes the right lymphatic duct as draining the right half of the body above the diaphragm through the right jugular trunk, right bronchomediastinal trunk and right subclavian trunk. It also notes that thoracic-duct obstruction can cause chylothorax, with obstruction below T5 tending to produce a right pleural effusion and obstruction above T5 a left pleural effusion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with gastric cancer and Virchow's node developed a left-sided pleural effusion. An intercostal chest tube was inserted, and the following fluid was drained. Where does the structure affected in this case normally drain into?

options.text: Junction of superior vena cava and left brachiocephalic veins
Junction of left jugular and left subclavian veins

questions.correctAnswerText: Junction of left jugular and left subclavian veins
questions.explanation: The fluid shown is chyle, indicating chylothorax from thoracic-duct obstruction. The thoracic duct normally drains into the junction of the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins. Gastric-cancer metastasis to the left supraclavicular Virchow node can mechanically obstruct the thoracic duct near its venous termination and produce a left-sided chylous effusion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Identify the level of the cross-section shown in the image below.
questions.explanation: The section is at T3-T4. It shows the large vascular opening of the aortic arch together with the openings of its three major branches: brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid artery and left subclavian artery. At T1-T2/T2-T3 only smaller branch-vessel openings are expected, while the T4-T5 plane is where the arch begins/ends and the pulmonary trunk bifurcation is visible.
